title: Ionospheric Scintillation Induced by Hot Flow Anomalies via Particle Precipitation
abstract: Ionospheric scintillation disrupts trans‐ionospheric radio signals and represents significant challenges for critical communication and navigation systems. Here we document that hot flow anomalies (HFAs), transient disturbances formed near Earth's bow shock, can contribute to scintillation near the cusp. We used coordinated multi‐instrument observations including GNSS receivers, SuperDARN, AMPERE, DMSP/SSUSI, MMS to link an upstream HFA to the scintillation in the polar ionosphere. During 10:47–10:57 UT on 19 November 2015, enhanced phase scintillation was observed, along with a convection vortex, enhanced field‐aligned currents (FACs) and nearby particle precipitation. An HFA and associated high‐speed jets (HSJs) were observed in the corresponding magnetic local time (MLT) region of the magnetosheath. Our analysis indicates that the HFA disturbs the magnetopause and enhances the FACs, causing the localized ionospheric density gradient instability, thereby triggering the ionospheric scintillation. These results show that the particle precipitation caused by HFAs can strongly affect the cusp plasma and trigger significant phase scintillation. Our results provided direct observational evidence that HFAs are a contributing source of polar space‐weather impacts on GNSS and radio systems.

title: Summer Marginal Ice Zone: A Potential Predictor for September Arctic Sea Ice Extent
abstract: The Arctic summer marginal ice zone (MIZ) represents a growing fraction of total sea ice extent (SIE), yet its predictive performance for September Arctic sea ice remains unknown. This study reveals that summer (June–August) MIZ area fraction is an optimal predictor for September Arctic SIE, particularly after 2000, with better forecast skill (S = 0.66) than summer Arctic SIE (S = 0.48). Gridded binary MIZ fields alone accurately predict September sea ice coverage (accuracy: 0.80–0.93), but overestimate the extent near the ice edge. Integrating gridded binary MIZ metrics, ice thickness, northward ice velocity, sea surface temperature, and net surface heat flux in peripheral seas mitigates such positive biases, with precision increasing by 0.09. This work highlights summer MIZ properties as key predictors for September sea ice, with predictive performance substantially improved by incorporating additional ice and oceanic variables.

title: Revisiting and Improving Soil Surface Resistance Schemes for Land Surface Modeling
abstract: Accurate representation of soil evaporation is critical for understanding land‐atmosphere interactions and improving climate simulations, where soil surface resistance plays a key regulatory role. However, existing schemes differ substantially and lack systematic evaluation. We compared five typical schemes and found large discrepancies in soil surface resistance values and site‐level simulations. Under intermediate soil wetness, different schemes showed over tenfold differences and had differing sensitivity parameters. Incorporating these schemes into the Common Land Model (CoLM) markedly altered soil wetness, evaporation, energy fluxes and ecosystem productivity, with mean soil wetness increasing by approximately 5%–35% and evaporation decreasing by approximately 9%–73% in summer. Using FLUXNET data and machine learning (XGBoost), we identified sand volume fraction as a key driver of β (a factor reflecting evaporation suppression calculated from soil resistance, with smaller values indicating stronger suppression). Building on Sellers et al. (1992, https://doi.org/10.1029/92jd01096) (S92), widely adopted for its simplicity and effectiveness in simulating latent heat flux and soil moisture, we incorporated this parameter to develop S92_sand, which better reproduced observation‐derived β than the typical schemes. When implemented in CoLM, S92_sand reduced mean absolute error and root mean square error (RMSE) of soil wetness by approximately 10% at evaporation‐dominant sites compared to S92. Regional assessments across China using GLEAM v4.2a demonstrated its superiority over the original S92 scheme, mitigating systematic overestimation of soil evaporation and reducing RMSE across 90% of the region, with improvements up to 1 mm day−1 over the Qinghai‐Tibet Plateau and the North China Plain. The simulations of soil wetness and evapotranspiration also showed noticeable regional improvements. This study provides new insights into soil surface resistance and advances land surface modeling of soil evaporation.

title: Assessing Co‐Located NISAR and Sentinel‐1 Observations for Atmospheric Characterization
abstract: Tropospheric delay remains one of the largest sources of uncertainty in repeat‐pass Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) measurements, while accurate three‐dimensional deformation retrieval continues to be limited by the geometry of current spaceborne SAR systems. The recent availability of near‐simultaneous observations from the NASA‐ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission and Sentinel‐1 provides a unique opportunity to investigate atmospheric signals using independent sensors observing nearly the same scene within minutes of each other. We analyze colocated NISAR L‐band and Sentinel‐1 C‐band interferometric observations over four regions spanning flat and mountainous terrain with varying vegetation cover. After applying the ionospheric correction provided in NISAR GUNW products, the residual NISAR interferometric phase exhibits strong agreement with corresponding Sentinel‐1 observations, with Pearson correlations exceeding 0.9 in several cases. The similarity between the two data sets suggests that both systems are observing a common atmospheric signal, which is interpreted primarily as tropospheric delay for the short (12‐day) interferometric intervals considered here. In contrast, tropospheric correction layers provided in the NISAR products often fail to reproduce the dominant spatial variability observed in either data set, particularly over flat terrain. These results demonstrate the potential of colocated NISAR and Sentinel‐1 observations for future evaluation of atmospheric correction products and motivate the development of multi‐frequency, multi‐geometry approaches for improved atmospheric characterization and three‐dimensional deformation estimation.

title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
abstract:
Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits. 
 In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits. Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits.

title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
abstract:
The authors show that, when detecting the presence of tactile stimuli, mouse primary somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decisions through the midbrain superior colliculus, primarily by shifting decision bias rather than the ability to detect the stimulus. 
 Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions. The authors show that, when detecting the presence of tactile stimuli, mouse primary somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decisions through the midbrain superior colliculus, primarily by shifting decision bias rather than the ability to detect the stimulus.

title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
abstract:
Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) cause aggressive DMGs by preventing radial glial progenitor cell differentiation into oligodendrocytes. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state. 
 Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1, co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state.

title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
abstract:
This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement. 
 Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope (https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus. This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.

title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
abstract:
Mentalising is essential for social interaction and is thought to rely on the medial prefrontal cortex. Here, the authors show that damage to the medial prefrontal cortex leaves mentalising intact but alters how quickly people make social decisions. 
 Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact. Mentalising is essential for social interaction and is thought to rely on the medial prefrontal cortex. Here, the authors show that damage to the medial prefrontal cortex leaves mentalising intact but alters how quickly people make social decisions.

title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
abstract:
Dinosaurs coexisted with flowering plants, but it’s unclear whether they ate them. The study presents a new small theropod dinosaur with remarkable jaw adaptations for eating fruit, providing one of the strongest evidence of dinosaur-angiosperm interaction. 
 The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi—the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear. Dinosaurs coexisted with flowering plants, but it’s unclear whether they ate them. The study presents a new small theropod dinosaur with remarkable jaw adaptations for eating fruit, providing one of the strongest evidence of dinosaur-angiosperm interaction.

title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
abstract:
Fuel cells rely on catalysts made of metal nanoparticles, but tracking how these particles wear down individually has been difficult. Here, the authors build an automated image analysis pipeline to track hundreds of platinum-cobalt nanoparticles and classify the degradation pathways they undergo. 
 Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale. Fuel cells rely on catalysts made of metal nanoparticles, but tracking how these particles wear down individually has been difficult. Here, the authors build an automated image analysis pipeline to track hundreds of platinum-cobalt nanoparticles and classify the degradation pathways they undergo.

title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
abstract:
Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition. 
 The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency. Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition.

title: Limited agricultural gains but high flood risk from global wetland reclamation
abstract:
As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation. 
 In recent decades, wetland reclamation for agricultural cultivation has remained as one solution to meet rising food demand; however, its agricultural benefits and broader sustainability implications are poorly understood. Here we identify wetland-reclaimed croplands (WRC) globally from 2000 to 2022 and assess their crop production performance and flood exposure risk. Results show that nearly half of WRC exhibited lower crop yields than existing croplands, especially when cultivated with upland crops. WRC contributed only 0.1% to total crop production, yet more than half faced severe flood hazards, with an average flood exposure probability 23 times higher than that of all croplands. Globally, 60% of WRC are subject to dual vulnerabilities of limited agricultural gains and high flood exposure, especially in food-importing or low-income countries. These findings reveal the unsustainability of wetland reclamation as an agricultural expansion strategy and underscore the pressing need to reconcile food security with wetland conservation. As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation.

title: Onset of zircon decomposition during saprolitic weathering
abstract:
Zircon is altered during saprolitic weathering through dissolution-precipitation reactions, during which U, Th, and REEs are incorporated into the zircon structure, enhancing metamictization and facilitating progressive zircon dissolution, according to geochemical analysis. 
 Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. However, how refractory zircon is during weathering, especially when crystalline and in an early stage of weathering, is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that crystalline zircon would start to weather during an early-stage saprolitic weathering. Nano-scale examination reveals that weathering of zircon proceeds through dissolution of primary, crystalline zircon and precipitation of secondary, amorphous zircon. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon. Zircon is altered during saprolitic weathering through dissolution-precipitation reactions, during which U, Th, and REEs are incorporated into the zircon structure, enhancing metamictization and facilitating progressive zircon dissolution, according to geochemical analysis.

title: Assessing the potential and cost of enhanced rock weathering in China
abstract:
Enhanced rock weathering contributes 5 to 30 percent of China’s negative emissions needs by 2060 at a net cost of 127 to 226 dollars per tonne of carbon dioxide removed, according to a spatially explicit grid-level analysis of croplands using basalt application scenarios 
 Large-scale carbon dioxide removal is essential for carbon neutrality, but current options face constraints. Enhanced rock weathering is a promising alternative, yet its viability at a national scale in China remains unquantified. Here we show, using a spatially explicit analysis across China’s croplands, that a single-year basalt application could remove 0.44–0.79 billion tonnes of CO2 by 2100, at a net life-cycle-adjusted cost of 127–226 US dollars per tonne of CO2 removed. Particles finer than those typically used commercially provide the most favorable balance between removal potential and cost. Multi-year application has the potential to contribute 5–30% of China’s negative emissions needs by 2060, with priority areas in Northeast, Central-South, and East China. title: Land-atmosphere feedback amplifies circulation-dominant fire weather risk over eastern Siberia
abstract:
Atmospheric circulation dominates the increase in fire weather risk over eastern Siberia in the past two decades, with circulation-triggered land-atmosphere feedbacks amplifying about 42% of that effect, as suggested by attribution of vapor pressure deficit based on reanalysis data. 
 Wildfires in eastern Siberia have intensified significantly in recent decades. This intensification is closely linked to rising vapor pressure deficit (VPD), a key indicator of fire weather risk. Previous studies have shown that atmospheric circulation increases VPD through subsidence-induced warming and drying, but the extent to which the circulation-driven VPD increase is realized through land–atmosphere feedback remains unclear. Here we show that atmospheric circulation explains about 60% of the 2004–2024 summer VPD trend over eastern Siberia, while circulation-triggered land-atmosphere feedback provides a major amplification pathway, accounting for about 42% of the circulation contribution. Mechanistically, reduced Laptev sea ice concentration favors a regional anomalous anticyclonic circulation over eastern Siberia, suppressing precipitation and depleting soil moisture. The resulting soil drying shifts surface energy from latent toward sensible heat, further amplifying regional VPD. These findings reveal a key land-surface pathway through which circulation intensifies fire weather risk and provide a broader framework for understanding similar changes in other fire-prone regions. Atmospheric circulation dominates the increase in fire weather risk over eastern Siberia in the past two decades, with circulation-triggered land-atmosphere feedbacks amplifying about 42% of that effect, as suggested by attribution of vapor pressure deficit based on reanalysis data.

title: Arctic climate tipping points under delayed CO<sub>2</sub> emissions mitigation
abstract:
Collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and abrupt Arctic cooling only occur when a delayed CO2 emission cessation happens after the exceedance of the 2∘C global mean temperature target, while in other scenarios the Arctic maintains warming trend, as suggested by idealized zero-emission model experiments. 
 The Arctic is warming more than three times faster than the global average – driven by increasing CO2 emissions – yet its response to the cessation of these emissions remains uncertain. We analyze 6-member ensembles of an Earth system model in which CO2 emissions are set instantaneously to zero at cumulative emission totals ranging from 800 to 2000 PgC. While global mean temperature stabilizes after CO2 emissions cessation, we find that the Arctic exhibits nonlinear and bifurcating behavior: either continued warming and sea-ice loss (below 1700 PgC), or abrupt cooling and sea-ice expansion (above 1700 PgC). The cooling results from a near-collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, causing reduced poleward ocean heat transport and amplifying lapse-rate and surface-albedo feedbacks. This collapse occurs when CO2 emission mitigation is delayed and global-mean temperature exceeds the 2∘C Paris Agreement target. Our results suggest stochastic tipping behavior modulated by the increased greenhouse gas forcing, triggering an abrupt transition to an alternative Arctic climate state. Collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation and abrupt Arctic cooling only occur when a delayed CO2 emission cessation happens after the exceedance of the 2∘C global mean temperature target, while in other scenarios the Arctic maintains warming trend, as suggested by idealized zero-emission model experiments.
